messages.content: Can you send to Mom an Email saying we should go out and play if Friday is okay.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to send emails directly. However, I can help you draft the message so you can copy it into your email client. Here’s a suggestion:

> Subject: Friday Outing?
>
> Hi Mom,
>
> I was thinking it would be fun to go out and play this Friday if that works for you. Let me know what you think!
>
> Love,
> [Your Name]

Feel free to tweak it as you like!
message.reasoning: The user wants to send an email to Mom. We need to use the function get_current_weather? No, that's unrelated. There's no function to send email. We cannot do that. We can respond that we can't send email.
